newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock funds still popular in April-firms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock funds still popular in April-firms.

text.p: Mutual fund investors continued to pour cash into U.S. stock index funds in April despite the volatility in the U.S. markets, but international stock funds were also popular, fund companies said Tuesday.

"Despite the market volatility at the beginning part of the month, at least here, investors stayed the course and continued to add to equity fund positions at the same pace they were in March," said Brian Mattes, a spokesman for Vanguard Group.

The stock market took investors for a roller coaster ride in April. The Dow continued to unwind from a record close of 7,085.16 set on March 11 and hit a low of 6,391.69 on April 11 before rebounding in the second half and close on Tuesday within sight of 7,000 again.

Tracey Gordon, a spokeswoman for Charles Schwab & Co, which sells more than 2,000 funds from a wide variety of companies, said index and international funds were big sellers in April just as in March.
"The big categories are still the same - index and international," she said.

Inflows into stock funds sold by Schwab totalled $540 million in April, including $268 million in international stock funds and $184 million into index funds, up from $338 million into stock funds in March.
The Investment Company Institute reported on Tuesday that net new cash flow into U.S. stock mutual funds fell to $10.51 billion in March from $18.16 billion in February.

ICI said flows to stock funds in the first three months of 1997 totalled $57.75 billion, compared with $72.54 billion for the same period in 1996. Flows into money market funds slowed sharply in March to an inflow of just $872.4 million compared with inflows of $21.12 billion in February.
Vanguard's flows into stock funds in April matched the $1.8 million in March, Mattes said.

"The vast majority of the equity flows went into index funds," he said. "It looks like it may be as much as $1 billion of the $1.8 billion, which is fairly consistent with flows we have seen in the past."

In addition to the index funds, Vanguard International Growth Portfolio took in $75 million in April to boost its assets to $6 billion, and Vanguard Windsor II took in more than $200 million to boost its assets to $17.3 billion, Mattes said.
Fidelity Investments, which has been losing market share due to its poorly-performing U.S. stock funds, said it expected about $1 billion in inflows in April after a flat March.

"The majority of the top selling equity funds are lower volatility funds," said Fidelity spokeswoman Robyn Tice. "Most equity investers were interested in the conservative growth and income funds, but some invested in index and international funds," she said.

David O'Leary, president of Alpha Equity Research, said Fidelity's flagship Magellan Fund had outflows of $621 million for the month through April 28, after outflows of $2.35 billion in the first quarter.
